title: TSPRank: Bridging Pairwise and Listwise Methods with a Bilinear Travelling Salesman Model

problem.claim: Pairwise LETOR methods can produce sub-optimal global rankings because they focus on pairwise comparisons.

gap.claim: Listwise deep-learning methods require complex tuning and yield only marginal improvements over robust pairwise models.

contributions.claim: Introduces TSPRank, a hybrid pairwise-listwise ranking method.
Reframes ranking as a Travelling Salesman Problem to model pairwise relationships and derive a listwise ranking through combinatorial optimisation.
Provides TSPRank as an additional component that can be integrated with embeddings from existing backbone models.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments across three backbone models and tasks involving stock ranking, information retrieval, and historical events ordering reportedly show that TSPRank significantly outperforms pure pairwise and listwise methods.
Qualitative analysis reportedly identifies better use of global information during ranking as TSPRank's main advantage over existing methods.
The authors report robustness and superior performance across different domains.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pairwise LETOR methods may yield sub-optimal global rankings because they focus on pairwise comparisons.
Listwise deep-learning methods have complex tuning requirements and only marginally improve over robust pairwise models.
TSPRank combines pairwise and listwise ranking by formulating ranking as a Travelling Salesman Problem.
The method can be added to embeddings produced by existing backbone models.
The authors report improved performance, better use of global information, robustness, and cross-domain effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The method combines pairwise relationship modelling with combinatorial optimisation for listwise ranking.

interpretation.claim: A ranking system may benefit from separating local preference modelling from global ordering.

application.claim: For ranking tasks where local comparisons do not adequately capture global order, consider hybrid objectives that incorporate a global optimisation step.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when the additional combinatorial optimisation is preferable in computational cost or accuracy.
